chunk_text: I now detail below Atmakarka etc. obtainable from among the 7 planets viz the Sun to Saturn. Some say that Rahu will become a Karka when there is a state of similarity in terms of longitude between (two) planets. Yet some say that the 8 planets including Rahu will have to be considered irrespective of such a state.

Among the planets from the Sun etc., whichever has traversed the maximum number of degrees in a particular sign is called Atmakaraka. If the degrees are identical, the one with more minutes of arc is considered, and if minutes are also identical, the one with higher seconds of arc is considered. For Rahu, his longitude is deducted from 30 degrees in that particular sign. The Atmakaraka is the most important and has a prime say on the native, just as a king is the head of all affairs.

The other karakas, such as Putrakaraka and Amatyakaraka, cannot predominate over the Atmakaraka. If the Atmakaraka is adverse, other karakas cannot give their benefic effects fully. Similarly, if the Atmakaraka is favourable, other karakas cannot predominate with their malefic influences.

The planet next to Atmakaraka in terms of longitude is called Amatyakaraka. Following in descending order of longitude are Bhratru Karaka, Matru Karaka, Pitru Karaka, Putrakaraka, Gnati Karaka, and Streekaraka. These are the Chara Karakas or inconstant significators. If two planets have the same longitude, they both become the same karaka, creating a deficit. In such a case, the constant significator should be considered for the concerned relative.

The constant significators are as follows: The stronger of the Sun and Venus indicates the father. The stronger of the Moon and Mars indicates the mother. Mars denotes sister, brother-in-law, younger brother, and mother. Mercury rules maternal relatives. Jupiter indicates the paternal grandfather. Venus denotes the husband, and Saturn denotes sons. Ketu signifies the wife, father, mother, parents-in-law, and maternal grandfather.
